story_type: explosion on a cargo ship mid-Atlantic, pararescuemen dropped into the sea, foreign helicopter airlifts the injured a day later
hook: A blast hit this ship 1,300 miles out in the Atlantic.
narration: An explosion tore through this cargo ship, thirteen hundred miles out in the Atlantic.
The six hundred thirty five foot Tamar lost one seaman. Three more were badly hurt.
A New York Air National Guard rescue plane dropped seven pararescuemen and a boat into the sea beside her.
Pararescuemen are trained medics who parachute to patients when no helicopter can reach them.
They treated the injured on board. It took twenty four hours to get within range of a Portuguese helicopter.
[short pause] Then it came in low over the deck.
outcome: Three pararescuemen and the two critically injured sailors were airlifted off, and the sailors were flown to Portugal.

location_card.place: Mid-Atlantic, 1,300 miles east of Cape Cod

title: Ship explosion 1,300 miles out at sea
description:
In April 2017, an explosion on the 635-foot bulk carrier Tamar far out in the Atlantic killed a seaman and badly injured others. The New York Air National Guard's 106th Rescue Wing dropped seven pararescuemen and a rescue boat beside the ship, and a Portuguese search and rescue helicopter later airlifted the two critically injured sailors.

Footage: U.S. Air National Guard video by Capt. Michael O'Hagan, New York National Guard, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/521558/tamar-rescue-sar-helo-extract
